There was no hack on Bitcoin - that's bullshit.

What's actually happening is that the transaction processing has slowed down some because there are some people out there sending shitloads of super tiny transactions (1/4 of one cent) to bog it up.

It's more like a very weak DDOS than a "hack", and can be worked around by anyone using Bitcoin by simply including a slightly larger transaction fee (little as 5 cents, compared to the like 2 cents or something it would suggest).

Ah Thank you! Who implements the transaction fee?

Also, why would increasing the fee stop the DDOS attack? Would it just make it cost more to continue the DDOS or is there a technical reason?

The transaction fee is chosen by the user making the transaction - whether or not its enough to get your transaction through as fast as you like is just based on competition with other users that may have chosen a higher fee. Some Bitcoin wallet clients can calculate an optimal fee, but that's a suggestion rather than being enforced on the user.

Increasing the fee you use when sending a transaction doesn't stop the DDOS - it just means that your transaction will be prioritized for inclusion in a block (a list of verified transactions) over ones with a lower, or no, fee.

Since the DDOS transactions have no fee, they will come after transactions sent with non-zero fees.

I know there's only about 30 of us here but what do you feel about an ARG run format and the or list? Personally I don't really think it impacts me all that much as I only play at my locals in Canada (no ARG here.) How do you guys feel about it?

Banlist for those who haven't seen it yet: http://articles.alterealitygames.com/announcing-the-arg-format/
What do you guys think of the ARG banlist?

I think it's bullshit. I agree with some of their ban list choices, but I don't like that

1) They don't tell who's making the decisions on the ban list. They only say "premier players". Presumably P. Hoban, Jeff Jones, and other ARG players and others who've won tournaments and events in the past, but we also don't know who had the final say. Without knowing who made the decision, we have no idea if there's bias for certain decks or players' opinions.

2) The players who had input on the ban list are being allowed to compete in the events. While those players have the most valuable input because they are meta players, they also are most likely to be biased towards a certain deck which may influence their decisions on what should and shouldn't be banned (e.g. Satellarknights are completely untouched by the list, despite a vocal outcry against them by many players). I do believe that the meta players should have input on a custom ban list, but whoever is making the final decisions should not be a competitor in these events or have close ties to competitors. (Konami prohibits anybody involved in the development of the game or the banlist and their families from competing in Tier 2 events, for example). Moreover, those players involved in the ban list's conception will know about the list much sooner than their competitors, giving them ample time to test the format. This gives ARG's players a very powerful edge, even without considering how those players may have influenced the ban list itself.

3) ARG has a hand in the secondary market, and if their ban list becomes popular they would be able to directly influence prices via the ban list. Many ARG players were allegedly stockpiling Tellarknight cards at Nats, and then this ban list was revealed which seems to favor Tellarknights over the other meta decks. In the stock market, such behavior is akin to insider trading, except in this case ARG has complete control over the ban list and can directly influence the prices of individual cards.

Thankfully, ARG is just testing the idea of a custom list right now. There are only 4 events IIRC that will have this list in effect, and there will be other events at the same time using Konami's official ban list. If ARG's list never takes off, then all of this is a non-issue. However, these events offer cash prizes of at least $1k each, so there's a good chance that the list could be successful despite the problems with how it was created. If that's the case, even players who aren't involved in ARG events will be affected because the secondary market will be influenced by the new ban lists thanks to our old friend supply and demand.

In other words, I don't like it. If ARG is going to make a ban list, they need to be completely transparent and fair in how and why the list was created.

No one is going to play by their list except for their own tournaments. People won't be willing to pay for cards for a banlist that exists outside of what everyone else is playing. Sell ARG stock NOW!!!!
I'm ok for it being a local situation, but not on a national level. Too much price manipulation if the list gets popular.

I feel like a lot of people are whining about it for no reason. ARG specifically said it would only be used on certain events of theirs. A very small number of them. So all the cries of "it's going to split the community!" and "they're trying to manipulate card prices!" are completely unfounded.

I'm personally happy that there's a new banlist to mess with. Variety is a good thing. Magic has several formats, and now Yugioh has a new one. I see no reason to get all butthurt about it.
ARG has a hand in the secondary market. This banlist can control the secondary market. I don't think I need to say more.
